messages:
ashley: Heads-up — noticed a 2.6x tail-latency spike on small-batch chat runs after the cuBLASLt update this morning. nsys trace attached (no title, just inline notes).

kai: repro script? which model / sequence length?

ashley: repro is on local prod-ish weight: 8 heads, head_dim=64, seq=128, batch=2. Mostly decoder-only chat path. The spike shows up when KV cache is warm and batching heuristic merges a cached prefix with a new request.

matt: can you paste the nsys kernel timeline? small screenshot is fine.

ashley: pasted timeline -> https://perf-uploads.internal/1832501111/nsys-timeline.png 

ashley: TL;DR from nsys: lots of calls into cublasLtMatmul with algo_id 0 and occasional cublasGemmEx fallback. The hotspots are cutlass_gemm kernels but with longer-than-expected workspace_allocs and queuing delays.

perf-bot: perf regression detected: 2.6x p99 increase vs baseline 1829000000. Tags: cuBLASLt, kvcache, batching-heuristic.

lina: interesting — workspace size negotiation failing maybe? cuBLASLt probes several algos and picks one requiring >64KB workspace but allocator returns smaller slab -> fallback to algo0 which is slower. Do we have logs from cublasLt algo selection?

ashley: yes, attached snippet from our tracing (copied):
```
[cuBLASLt] probe algos for matmul (M=256, N=64, K=2048)
algo 0: workspace_needed=0, time=8.2us
algo 1: workspace_needed=131072, time=1.9us
algo 2: workspace_needed=65536, time=2.3us
selected: algo0 (workspace insufficient)
```

kai: that explains it. When kv cache merges, effective K spikes (concatenated cache) so some probes request big workspace. Our slab allocator currently enforces per-stream max workspace=48KB for small requests to avoid fragmentation. That was tuned for throughput but regressed these shapes.

matt: can we reproduce with a forced allocator bump? e.g., export REDWOOD_CUBLASLT_MAX_WORKSPACE=196608 and re-run?

ashley: tried that locally — p99 drops back to baseline. Patch: set stream-local max workspace to 256KB for matmuls where K>1024.

lina: uh, but that could increase memory pressure during heavy batching. Need guarded change: only bump when kvcache-merged and batch size <=4. Also add a slow-path fallback counter so we can alert if we thrash.

kai: logging idea: emit probe outcome metric: (selected_algo, workspace_granted, probe_time_us). We can then alert if selected_algo==0 and workspace_granted<requested.

matt: agree. Also add a small nvprof/nsys smoke job in our CI that runs a sequence of shapes (K:512,1024,2048,4096) and asserts no >2x regression on p99. Put it behind a perf gate.

ashley: created quick PR with allocator tweak + probe metric instrumentation. Link: https://git.internal/r/PR/1423 — includes nsys collection script (see tests/prof/nstest.sh) and an example perfetto json.

perf-bot: ci/perf-smoke failed on PR 1423 (nsys capture mismatch).

lina: I'll take the CI trace. Can you add a tiny reproducer that toggles KV cache merge on/off? Makes it easier to compare.

ashley: added a toggle flag and a short perfetto example. Re-ran locally, attached both traces. perfetto shows kernel enqueue stalls at the moment the allocator blocks waiting for larger slab.

kai: next steps: (1) land probe metrics + alert, (2) conservative allocator bump for merge-case only, (3) add CI nsys smokejob, (4) monitor memory tail.

matt: also add a short note to eng-runtime runbook about this class of regression (kvcache-induced K growth -> workspace negotiation failure). Saves future debugging time.

ashley: filed an ops note and added a line in runbook. I'll send the PR with tests w/ perf-bot once ci/perf-smoke is green. Thanks all :thumbsup:

lina: nice work finding the root cause quickly. If perf-bot still flaps after the allocator change, we may need to implement an adaptive reclamation (e.g., evict tiny slabs) or prefer streaming GEMM for extreme K values.

ashley: noted. Will follow up if we hit memory pressure.

matt: saving traces to s3://perf/eng-runtime/1832501111/ for later reference.

ashley: closing loop — PR merged, metrics in prod, adding alert to pagerduty if selected_algo==0 rate > 10% over 5m for top routes.

kai: excellent.
